key_insight: Asymmetric contrastive pre-training can transfer longitudinal EHR representations across countries by grouping patients with the same target outcome without forcing unrelated negative trajectories together.
clinical_relevance: This could help build stronger few-shot and cross-institution prediction models when local labeled data are limited and coding systems differ.
method: Pre-trained temporal Transformer encoders on 3.98 million patients from Taiwan’s NHIRD.
Used a hybrid vocabulary-mapping pipeline combining direct concept matches with embedding-based retrieval to bridge NHIRD and U.S. EHR vocabularies.
Compared Asymmetric SupCon against standard contrastive learning and initialization baselines on MIMIC-IV and EHRSHOT.
evidence_signal: Transferred models improved over random initialization on MIMIC-IV, showed especially strong few-shot performance on EHRSHOT incident disease prediction, and Asymmetric SupCon achieved the best AUPRC on 3 of 4 tasks.
watch_item: Cross-national transfer depends on semantic mapping quality and may not generalize equally well across all clinical tasks or data infrastructures.
paper_title: Bridging the EHR Divide: Asymmetric Contrastive Learning for Cross-National Medical Representation Transfer
